content: styrened has three separate systems touching hub/network settings: (1) core-config.yaml reticulum/config for TCP interfaces, (2) HubConnection for LXMF propagation destination tracking, (3) TUI first-run config generator with hardcoded template

The LXMF hub destination hash (6fc8bf22aa293588c9bf8d7488102e95) is hardcoded and separate from TCP transport interfaces - HubConnection.connect() uses RNS.Transport.has_path()/request_path() for LXMF store-and-forward, not for establishing TCP connections
RNS TCPClientInterface peers are defined in core-config.yaml under reticulum.interfaces.peers, then generate_rns_config() writes them to ~/.reticulum/config which RNS reads at startup

Planned Network tab scope: peer list management (add/remove/edit TCPClientInterface entries), AutoInterface on/off toggle, transport mode (standalone/shared, enable_transport), all writing back to core-config.yaml and regenerating ~/.reticulum/config
get_profile_defaults() seeds config.reticulum.interfaces.peers with rns.styrene.io:4242 as a TCPClientInterface stanza
styrened uses async-first architecture with asyncio event loop, periodic tasks for announces and cleanup
CI/CD runs on Argo Workflows on brutus K3s cluster, triggered by Argo Events GitHub webhooks. GitHub Actions removed.

Settings screen Network tab redesign is in progress: removing hub selector/KNOWN_HUBS/STYRENE_HUB_ADDRESS UI, replacing with TCPClientInterface peer manager (add/remove/edit), AutoInterface toggle, transport mode (DeploymentMode enum), and server interface config. Save writes both core-config.yaml and regenerates ~/.reticulum/config.

CoreConfig model includes DeploymentMode enum (STANDALONE, HUB, etc.), PeerConfig (host, port, name), ServerInterfaceConfig (enabled, listen_ip, port), and InterfaceConfig (peers list, auto bool, server) under config.reticulum.interfaces
Config validation via validate_core_config() returns errors with field names — validates peer host non-empty, port in valid range, and hub mode requiring server or peer interfaces
Config serialization uses _serialize_config() which converts CoreConfig to dict; PeerConfig entries without a name omit the name key from serialized output

Settings screen Network tab now has 5 panels: TRANSPORT (mode, enable_transport, announce_interval), PEERS (dynamic add/remove TCPClientInterface rows), LOCAL DISCOVERY (AutoInterface toggle), SERVER (TCPServerInterface enable/IP/port), BATMAN-ADV MESH (existing mesh settings)
Settings save now persists network config to both core-config.yaml (via save_core_config) AND regenerates ~/.reticulum/config (via generate_rns_config + write_text) so RNS picks up changes on restart
KNOWN_HUBS dict, hub_select widget, custom hub address input, and hub announce interval have been removed from the settings screen - replaced by the interface manager panels

The LXMF hub address, hub selector (KNOWN_HUBS), and hub_announce_interval fields have been removed from the TUI settings screen as part of the Network tab redesign. Hub/propagation is handled separately from the interface manager.
Peer list in Network tab now has column headers (Name/Host/Port) rendered as a .peer-header-row of Static widgets with .peer-header CSS class above the dynamic peer rows

styrene --upgrade CLI runs pipx upgrade styrene (or pip install --upgrade) then pkill -f styrened daemon. styrene --reset backs up configs as .bak, regenerates core-config.yaml and ~/.reticulum/config from defaults, and kills daemon.

TUI app's _show_upgrade_screen callback calls _restart_tui() which uses os.execvp to re-exec the process. _restart_tui() finds the styrene entry point (argv0 or shutil.which), calls self.exit(), then registers atexit handler to exec after Textual teardown.

UpgradeScreen upgrade flow: _build_upgrade_cmd() detects pipx vs pip and uses --upgrade-strategy=eager to force transitive dep upgrades. _do_upgrade() runs subprocess in @work thread with 120s timeout, streams output to Log widget, then kills daemon via pkill. Dismiss returns bool to app callback.

Settings screen tab navigation uses [ and ] screen-level keyboard bindings that delegate to TabbedContent.action_previous/next_tab, bypassing arrow key consumption by Input widgets inside tab panes (v0.10.46)

UpgradeScreen._build_upgrade_cmd() passes --upgrade-strategy=eager for both pipx and pip paths. For pipx, uses '--pip-args=--upgrade-strategy=eager' as single combined argument (fixed from two separate args that pipx couldn't parse).

RNS interfaces have .online attribute for connection status, accessible via RNS.Transport.interfaces — rns_service._log_interface_status() and _last_interface_states dict track UP/DOWN state changes at runtime

TUI has 19+ files with inline CSS (CSS = or DEFAULT_CSS =): screens (upgrade, contacts, conversation, exploration, inbox, provision, confirm_flash, mesh_device_detail) and widgets (chat_widget, config_form, activity_feed, node_info_panel, hardware_panel, message_bubble, image_preview, uptime_panel, highlighted_panel, page_browser, forge_log). Main theme CSS lives in imperial_crt.tcss.

Textual ColorSystem has limited built-in theme variables (primary, secondary, warning, error, success, accent, foreground, background, surface, panel, boost, text_alpha). Custom variables are added via the 'variables' dict parameter. styrene_brand.py adds: border, border-blurred, block-cursor-*, footer-*, input-*, scrollbar*, and text-muted.

Settings screen uses Switch (not Checkbox) for all toggles as of v0.10.52. Switch renders as a sliding toggle. CSS class .setting-checkbox styles it borderless/transparent/compact. Save handler queries Switch widgets, not Checkbox. Tests use Switch import.

Custom Textual theme variable $text-muted added to styrene_brand.py ColorSystem variables dict, mapped to STYRENE_DARK['muted_foreground'] (#9ca3af) — provides readable muted text color for descriptions and headers. Used in imperial_crt.tcss for .setting-description and .peer-header.

TUI scrollbar architecture (v0.10.54): Screen-level global scrollbar rules (scrollbar-background:$surface, scrollbar-color:$border, size:1). Blanket transparent background rule for VerticalScroll/ScrollableContainer/RichLog/Log/TextArea. Individual widgets (ActivityFeed, ForgeLog, ChatWidget) have explicit scrollbar styling in DEFAULT_CSS. All scrollable containers must set background+scrollbar-track+scrollbar-thumb.

styrene-pypi sync-version.yml now builds and publishes to PyPI directly (not via release event cascade). GITHUB_TOKEN-created releases cannot trigger other workflows (GitHub anti-cascade). The workflow: detect new styrened on PyPI → bump pyproject.toml → commit+tag → build wheel → publish to PyPI → create GitHub release. Cron hourly + repository_dispatch from Argo.
Local PyPI publish path added: justfile 'publish' recipe runs .venv/bin/python -m build + .venv/bin/python -m twine upload dist/* for immediate availability instead of waiting for Argo CI

Argo release-build.yaml uses twine upload --skip-existing, so local pre-publishing via 'just publish' doesn't break the Argo pipeline — it silently skips the already-uploaded wheel and continues to OCI build and GitHub Release steps

RNS announce callback chain is being investigated to determine if the receiving interface name is available in announce handlers — needed for correlating discovered devices to their source hub/peer for hierarchical display

RNS announce handler callback signature is fixed at 3-5 params (destination_hash, announced_identity, app_data, announce_packet_hash, is_path_response) — receiving interface is NOT passed to handlers. However, RNS.Transport.path_table[destination_hash][5] stores the receiving_interface object post-announce, with .name attribute matching config stanza name.

RNS.Transport dispatches announce handlers via inspect.signature() parameter count detection (3, 4, or 5 params) and runs each handler in a separate daemon thread via threading.Thread(target=job, daemon=True).start()

NodeStore SQLite schema uses ALTER TABLE migrations for new columns (try/except OperationalError pattern) — lxmf_destination_hash, short_name, system_fingerprint were added this way. Same pattern will be used for discovered_via column.

Dashboard screen replaced flat MeshDeviceTable(DataTable) with MeshDeviceTree(Tree) widget that groups discovered devices hierarchically by their discovered_via interface name. Interface branches are auto-expanded, leaf nodes carry device identity as data for selection/navigation.

MeshDevice.discovered_via field populated in StyreneAnnounceHandler.received_announce() by looking up RNS.Transport.path_table[destination_hash][5].name — index 5 is the receiving interface object with a .name attribute matching the config stanza name.

NodeStore 'nodes' table has discovered_via TEXT column (ALTER TABLE migration pattern) with idx_discovered_via index. UPSERT uses COALESCE(excluded.discovered_via, nodes.discovered_via) to preserve existing interface info when new announce lacks it.

Hierarchical mesh device tree implemented in dashboard — MeshDeviceTree(Tree) widget replaces flat DataTable, grouping discovered devices under their source interface (e.g., 'Styrene Community Hub' branch → child devices, 'Direct / Unknown' → devices without interface info). Uses MeshDevice.discovered_via field populated from RNS.Transport.path_table[dest_hash][5].name post-announce.

NodeStore has 'paths' table with interface_type and interface_name columns per destination_hash. The 'nodes' table now has a discovered_via TEXT column (added via ALTER TABLE migration) with idx_discovered_via index for efficient dashboard Tree grouping. UPSERT uses COALESCE to preserve existing interface info.

DashboardScreen event handling changed from on_data_table_row_selected(DataTable.RowSelected) to on_tree_node_selected(Tree.NodeSelected[str]) for device detail navigation. Tree node .data carries device identity string; None data on branch/empty nodes is ignored.

Dashboard MESH DEVICES panel uses Tree widget (MeshDeviceTree) instead of DataTable as of v0.10.59. Devices grouped by discovered_via interface name. MeshDevice.discovered_via populated from RNS.Transport.path_table[destination_hash][5].name in the announce handler (post-hoc lookup — RNS doesn't pass interface to announce callbacks). nodes table has discovered_via column + idx_discovered_via index. COALESCE preserves existing value when re-announce has no interface info.

NodeInfoPanel renders in two-column layout as of v0.10.61. Left column: SYSTEM (CPU/RAM/NET/STORAGE), DAEMON (IPC mode only), IDENTITY (name/alias/hash/PQC tier). Right column: RETICULUM (RNS status/uplink/interfaces), STYRENE (mode/hub/mesh count), VERSION (styrened __version__). Uses Rich markup with regex-based padding for side-by-side rendering within a single Static widget. render() delegates to _render_left_column() and _render_right_column() methods. Located at src/styrened/tui/widgets/node_info_panel.py.

HighlightedPanel (Vertical) composes: hp-top Static (1 line) + hp-content Vertical + hp-bottom Static (1 line). hp-content default is height:auto (safe for modals/settings). Dashboard panels (#mesh-devices-panel, #activity-feed-panel) override hp-content to height:1fr via CSS specificity. Box-drawing borders rendered via Rich markup with ColorCascade hex colors.
styrened TUI uses Textual 8.0.0 as of 2026-03-01

Two identity systems coexist: (1) RNS operator identity — cryptographic keypair at reticulum.operator_identity_path, identity hash for routing, (2) Styrene IdentityConfig — display_name, icon, short_name for human-readable appearance. Both stored in core-config.yaml under different sections (reticulum vs identity). Investigation ongoing to ensure they don't conflict.

YubiKey identity provider uses FIDO2 hmac-secret extension to derive deterministic 64-byte RNS identity (X25519 + Ed25519) from hardware token. Two application-specific salts (styrene-encryption-v1, styrene-signing-v1) produce independent 32-byte outputs via getAssertion. Credential ID stored in config as base64. Located at src/styrened/services/yubikey.py. Requires pip install styrened[yubikey] (python-fido2>=1.0).

Identity provider selection in _resolve_identity_path(): priority 0 is YubiKey (if identity_config.provider == 'yubikey'), then config override path, system /etc/styrene/identity, user ~/.config/styrene/identity, LXMF app detection, and finally new generation. YubiKey path calls derive_identity_bytes() and RNS.Identity.from_bytes() inline, returning hex hash directly without writing to disk.

get_operator_identity() and get_operator_identity_object() now delegate to _load_identity_config() which loads IdentityConfig from core-config.yaml, then check provider field. YubiKey provider calls derive_identity_bytes() inline; file provider falls through to _resolve_identity_path() + from_file(). get_operator_identity() wraps get_operator_identity_object() with hash extraction and exception handling.

Well-known RNS community hubs include: dublin.connect.reticulum.network:4965 (Dublin Hub), reticulum.betweentheborders.com:4242 (BetweenTheBorders), istanbul.reserve.network:9034, node01.rns.bnz.se:4242, rns.stoppedcold.com:4242, rtclm.de:4242, sydney.reticulum.au:4242. These are being added alongside rns.styrene.io:4242 as default/selectable peer interfaces.

PeerConfig model now has an 'enabled' field (default True) — parsed from core-config.yaml via _parse_bool(p.get('enabled', True)), serialized as 'enabled' key in _serialize_config(), and used by generate_rns_config() to skip disabled peers (continue if not peer.enabled).

TUI peer rows replaced static status indicator (● dot with CSS color classes) with a Switch toggle (peer_enabled_{i}) that controls the PeerConfig.enabled field. Switch uses .setting-checkbox and .peer-enabled-toggle CSS classes. Peer enabled state persists to core-config.yaml and controls whether the peer is written to ~/.reticulum/config.

WELL_KNOWN_HUBS constant defined in models/config.py — list of 5 PeerConfig entries (Styrene Community Hub enabled, 4 community hubs disabled by default). Used by both daemon (services/config.py) and TUI (tui/services/config.py) config generators to seed new installs.

Config loaders (daemon services/config.py and TUI tui/services/config.py) merge missing WELL_KNOWN_HUBS as disabled entries after parsing peers list. Keyed by (host, port) tuple to avoid duplicates. Existing peers are never modified — only missing hubs are appended with enabled=False. This ensures existing installs see well-known hubs in Settings without manual addition.

MeshDeviceTree CSS changed in latest fix: .tree--cursor background changed from $surface to $background (eliminates visible gray shadow bar on selected row), .tree--highlight changed from $background to transparent (hover no longer shows background change). Selected row identified by $primary color + bold text only.

StyreneConfig.identity is a property that proxies to StyreneConfig.core.identity. The TUI load path calls _overlay_core_identity() which reads core config via load_core_config() and replaces config.core.identity with the loaded IdentityConfig. Settings screen Input widgets are populated from self.config.identity.display_name at compose() time.
No image/media handling exists in StyreneEnvelope wire protocol yet — image attachment support is greenfield. No content_type, attachment, or media fields in models/styrene_wire.py or protocols/.

Wire protocol image attachment design for StyreneEnvelope: MediaAttachment struct with content_type, data, original_type (for lossless JPEG repack tracking), thumbnail (progressive prefix), width, height. Defined in docs/image-format-assessment.md in styrene-rs repo. Vec<MediaAttachment> on envelope.

Image attachment design for StyreneEnvelope finalized: MediaAttachment(content_type, data, original_type, thumbnail, width, height). JXL as native format with JPEG fallback. original_type tracks lossless JPEG repacks for reversible extraction. Target 15-50KB per image. Progressive decode for mesh UX (2KB→1/8 res, 10KB→1/4 res, full). Design doc at styrene-rs/docs/image-format-assessment.md.

JXL Rust crate ecosystem (2026-03): jxl-oxide 0.12 (pure Rust decoder, active, modular sub-crates), zune-jpegxl 0.5 (pure Rust encoder, early), jxl-encoder 0.1 (pure Rust, early), jpegxl-rs 0.13 (libjxl C bindings). For styrene-mesh, jxl-oxide is primary decode, jpegxl-rs or zune-jpegxl for encode (TBD evaluation).

Python-Rust binding landscape: PyO3 (v0.23+, production-grade, standard choice — used by Polars, ruff, Pydantic V2) + Maturin (v1.8+, build backend for PyO3→wheels) is the clear winner. Also: pyo3-asyncio (Rust futures↔asyncio), rust-numpy (zero-copy ndarray), uniffi (Mozilla multi-lang IDL). Potential future use: styrene-imagecodecs PyO3 crate wrapping jxl-oxide to eliminate libjxl system dep for Python.

JXL lossless JPEG repack flow for Styrene: phone sends JPEG → Styrene wraps to JXL losslessly (20% smaller) with original_type='image/jpeg' → transmit over mesh → receiver can decode JXL or extract bit-exact original JPEG for non-Styrene clients. Zero quality loss, reversible.

Incremental Rust migration strategy via PyO3 FFI proposed in styrene-rs/docs/incremental-rust-migration.md. Two integration modes: (1) wire interop (independent Rust daemon over LXMF), (2) FFI hybrid (Rust modules exposed via PyO3 as styrene-native package, imported by Python daemon as drop-in replacements). Uses try/except ImportError pattern for graceful fallback to pure Python.

styrene-native PyO3 crate planned at crates/bindings/styrene-native/ — cdylib extension module built with maturin, re-exports from styrene-mesh/styrene-rns/styrene-lxmf crates. Installed via pip install styrened[native]. Falls back to pure Python when not installed.

Dual-path compatibility verification strategy: pytest fixture with params=['python','rust'] runs every test twice against both implementations. Any behavioral divergence caught immediately. Impossible with wire-only approach. Feature flag STYRENE_NATIVE=0 forces pure Python in production.

styrene-rs has two integration modes with styrened: (1) Wire interop — independent Rust daemon communicates over LXMF mesh (styrened-rs binary), (2) FFI hybrid — Rust modules exposed via PyO3 (styrene-native package) imported by Python daemon as drop-in replacements. Wire protocol (StyreneEnvelope in styrene-mesh crate) remains the shared contract for mode 1. Mode 2 enables incremental migration.

styrene-rs PARITY_GAPS.md shows ~37K Rust LOC across 6 crates with 212 tests. Missing service layer (~12K LOC): conversation service, auto-reply, node store persistence, remote terminal, protocol registry, file transfer, hub connection. Critical gaps: IFAC multi-hop bug, Serial/KISS interface, propagation store-and-forward, config system.

styrene-native PyO3 crate scaffolded at crates/bindings/styrene-native/ in styrene-rs repo. Cargo.toml defines cdylib crate type with pyo3 0.23 + extension-module feature, depending on styrene-mesh and styrene-rns path deps. pyproject.toml uses maturin>=1.0 build backend. Package name: styrene-native, lib name: styrene_native.

styrene-mesh crate's wire protocol uses StyreneMessage struct (not StyreneEnvelope) with encode()/decode() methods. Wire format: 10-byte namespace 'styrene.io' + 1-byte version (0x01) + 1-byte type enum + 16-byte request_id + variable msgpack payload. Header is 28 bytes. StyreneMessageType enum covers Control, Status, RPC Commands/Responses, Terminal Sessions, and PQC Sessions ranges.

Python styrened service layer LOC breakdown: reticulum.py 1407, conversation_service.py 1316, lxmf_service.py 1114, config.py 1075, node_store.py 986, doctor.py 753, rns_service.py 653, file_transfer.py 637, auto_reply.py 634, page_browser.py 524, hardware.py 518, pqc_session.py 424, attachment_store.py 359, hub_connection.py 342. Total services ~12.5K LOC. Models total ~17K LOC (styrene_wire.py alone is 1124).

StyreneApp.action_interrupt() implements double ctrl+c quit pattern: single ctrl+c pops screen stack toward dashboard, second ctrl+c within 1.0s window exits app. Uses time.monotonic() tracking via _last_interrupt class var. Binding uses priority=True to bypass focused widget key consumption.

LXMF propagation destination populated in TUI settings from config.core.lxmf.propagation_destination. Community Hub Switch toggle (#community_hub_enabled) auto-fills propagation_destination Input with COMMUNITY_HUB_PROPAGATION_HASH on enable, clears on disable (only if it matches the community hash). Empty propagation field despite enabled hub suggests config.core.lxmf.propagation_destination is None/empty at load time.

TUI config loading changed from _overlay_core_identity() (identity-only) to _overlay_core_config() which replaces entire config.core with load_core_config() result. This means core-config.yaml is the single source of truth for ALL CoreConfig fields (identity, reticulum, lxmf, rpc, discovery, api). tui.yaml still contains a stale copy of reticulum/rpc/etc sections that gets parsed then overwritten by the overlay.

_overlay_core_config() in tui/services/config.py replaces entire config.core with load_core_config() result. core-config.yaml is the single source of truth for all CoreConfig fields. Identity is stored in core-config.yaml, settings screen _save_identity() writes there first, then updates self.config.core.identity in memory so subsequent save_core_config() preserves new values.

MeshDeviceTree does NOT filter LOST nodes — all device statuses (ACTIVE, STALE, LOST) are displayed with different status symbols (● active, ◐ stale, ○ lost). Previous DataTable implementation filtered LOST nodes out.

_deduplicate_by_identity() in services/reticulum.py both deduplicates by identity_hash AND filters out devices with last_announce older than 30 minutes (cutoff = now - 1800). LOST devices are not filtered by status — they're filtered by age. Devices <30min old with LOST status still appear in the tree.

_parse_config_dict in tui/services/config.py now parses 'identity' and 'lxmf' sections from config.yaml/tui.yaml in addition to tui/fleet/provisioning/mesh/reticulum/rpc sections. Identity parsed only if display_name is non-empty (empty string keeps default 'Anonymous Styrene').

StyreneConfig._parse_config_dict parses: tui, fleet, provisioning, mesh, reticulum (interfaces/peers/hub), rpc, identity (display_name/icon/short_name if non-empty), and lxmf sections. Identity from config.yaml is now read but may be superseded by _overlay_core_config() if core-config.yaml has a real identity.

ContactsScreen DataTable was restructured: columns changed from ALIAS/PEER HASH/NOTES to ALIAS/STATUS/LAST MESSAGE/PEER HASH. Now cross-references IPCBridge get_devices() and get_conversations() to show live presence (● online, ◐ stale, ○ unknown) and last message preview with relative time. ContactInfo.to_dict() exists on the service DTO (services/contacts.py ContactInfo dataclass), not on the SQLAlchemy Contact model (models/contacts.py).

ContactInfo (services/contacts.py) is a dataclass DTO with to_dict() and from_model() methods. Contact (models/contacts.py) is the SQLAlchemy model with no to_dict(). These are two distinct classes — ContactService returns ContactInfo instances.

DeviceInfo (ipc/messages.py) has lxmf_destination_hash and destination_hash fields. ContactsScreen presence lookup matches contact peer_hash against both device fields to find the corresponding device.

styrened.tui.menubar subpackage added at src/styrened/tui/menubar/ — macOS menu bar agent showing unread count, recent conversations, and daemon status via rumps NSApplication loop. IPC polling runs in a background asyncio thread. Architecture: rumps event loop on main thread, asyncio IPC loop in daemon thread, shared state via MenuBarState dataclass with threading.Lock.
MenuBar agent uses osascript for native macOS notifications (display notification command via subprocess.Popen) rather than pyobjc or native APIs — lightweight, no additional deps.
ChatWidget._pending_attachment dict tracks staged attachments with keys: awaiting_path (bool), data_b64, filename, mime. Attachment sent on next message submission.
rumps added to pyproject.toml [tui] extras with sys_platform='darwin' marker. Import in agent.py still has friendly ImportError message as fallback.

Clipboard integration module added at src/styrened/tui/menubar/clipboard.py — reads image data and file references from macOS clipboard using PyObjC AppKit. Priority: PNG image data → TIFF image data → file URL references (Finder copy) → text that looks like a file path. Returns ClipboardAttachment dataclass with data_b64, filename, mime, size, source fields.

ChatWidget on_paste() handler detects clipboard image data (screenshots via NSPasteboardTypePNG/TIFF) before falling back to file path text. Calls _stage_from_clipboard() for image data, _stage_attachment_from_path() for path text. Supported path file types expanded beyond images to include pdf, txt, md, zip, tar, gz, mp3, wav, ogg, mp4, mov.

action_attach_file (a key) now tries clipboard first via read_clipboard_attachment() before prompting for a file path. action_paste_attachment (ctrl+v binding) explicitly stages clipboard content when widget is focused in message-browsing mode.

_stage_from_clipboard() async worker reads clipboard in executor, sets _pending_attachment dict, displays status with source label (📋 screenshot, 📋 copied image, 📎 file, 📎 path), and focuses chat input for optional message text.
pyobjc-core and pyobjc-framework-Cocoa 12.1 are already available in the styrened venv (pulled in by rumps dependency) — AppKit imports work without adding new deps.

ChatWidget action_attach_clipboard() calls _attach_from_clipboard_or_prompt() via run_worker — if clipboard read returns None, falls back to path prompt by setting awaiting_path:True and focusing the Input. Worker errors are not explicitly caught in on_worker_state_changed.

NodeInfoPanel _render_left_column() has sections: SYSTEM, COMMS (inbox unread, chats count, contacts count, auto-reply status), IDENTITY; _render_right_column() has sections: RETICULUM, STYRENE, TRAFFIC (msg sent/recv, pending, active links, transport/propagation roles), VERSION

NodeInfoPanel reactive vars for comms/traffic: unread_count, conversation_count, contact_count, messages_sent, messages_received, pending_deliveries, auto_reply_enabled, propagation_enabled, transport_enabled, active_links. _load_comms_data() populates from local SQLite DB in standalone mode; IPC bridge populates in daemon mode.
Dashboard panel CSS proportions (v0.12.0): #node-info-panel height:auto max-height:28, #mesh-devices-panel height:2fr min-height:6, #activity-feed-panel height:1fr min-height:4 max-height:16.
Exploration table has HOPS and VIA columns as of v0.12.1. HOPS from RNS.Transport.path_table[dest][2], VIA from discovered_via. Both sortable. MeshDevice model extended with optional hops field.

ChatWidget._last_displayed_date tracks the most recent date separator rendered, enabling date separator continuity across incremental message appends. _maybe_mount_date_separator() helper mounts a separator Static when the message date changes.

ChatWidget message format (v0.13.0): outgoing uses 'content icon HH:MM' right-padded (8-char left margin), incoming uses sender name on own line + 'content HH:MM' left-padded (8-char right margin). No 'ME:' prefix on outgoing. Position, color, and alignment differentiate sender.

RNS.Transport.path_table keys are bytes (raw destination hash bytes), not hex strings. Index 5 is receiving_interface object. This matches the existing implementation in StyreneAnnounceHandler which passes bytes destination_hash to path_table.get().

RNS.Transport.path_table entry index 1 (received_from) contains the next-hop transport node hash that relayed the announce — distinct from index 5 (interface) which is the local interface. Both are available for richer VIA display.

ExplorationScreen has a fifth 'Styrene' tab (tab-styrene) added before the existing 4 tabs, using StyreneFleetTable (DataTable subclass) instead of ReticumAnnounceTable, with columns NAME/VERSION/CAPABILITIES/HOPS/VIA/STATUS/LAST ANNOUNCE and Styrene-specific filtering/deduplication via _deduplicate_by_identity().

ExplorationScreen has five tabs (Styrene, LXMF, Pages, Infrastructure, Other). _EXPLORATION_TYPES excludes DeviceType.STYRENE_NODE from generic discovery. Styrene tab uses StyreneFleetTable with fleet-specific columns. ReticumAnnounceTable is shared by the other 4 tabs. _STYRENE_TYPES = frozenset({DeviceType.STYRENE_NODE}).

StyreneFleetTable (DataTable[str]) at exploration.py shows Styrene fleet nodes with columns NAME, VERSION, CAPABILITIES, HOPS, VIA, STATUS, LAST ANNOUNCE. Capability icons: 📨 autoreply, ⚡ exec, 🔌 rpc, 🔀 transport. Deduplicates via _deduplicate_by_identity(). Sortable by all columns. Has set_filter(), sort_by(), refresh_data() methods. Standalone mode reads from node_store.get_styrene_nodes() + discover_devices().

IPC CMD_RETRY_MESSAGE handler fully implemented in handlers.py: prepare_retry() → reset to PENDING → rebuild LXMF payload → send via lxmf_service.send_message() with delivery callbacks → register_delivery_tracking() → mark_sent(). Returns ErrorResponse.not_found if message not in FAILED state.

_resolve_identity() Strategy 5 implemented: requests RNS path + parallel identity_hash path request, then polls for up to 10s (0.5s sleep intervals) for identity to arrive via re-announce or path response. IPC handlers wrap send_message calls in run_in_executor to prevent event loop blocking during the 10s wait.

lxmf_service.send_message() returns None when: (1) LXMF not initialized, (2) _resolve_identity() returns None after exhausting 5 strategies: direct RNS recall, NodeStore operator dest lookup, NodeStore LXMF dest lookup, persistent storage load, Strategy 5 (request_path + 10s poll loop). Strategy 5 blocks calling thread up to 10s — IPC handlers call send_message via run_in_executor to isolate blocking. send timeout bumped to 30s in TUI.

MeshDeviceDetailScreen._resolve_nomadnet_destination() checks if the device is a NOMADNET_NODE directly, or queries NodeStore for any node with matching identity_hash and DeviceType.NOMADNET_NODE — enabling Pages tab for Styrene nodes that co-announce NomadNet aspects (same RNS identity, different destination hash).

NomadNet pages are a feature set of a Styrene node: same RNS identity produces separate destination hashes for different announce aspects — ('nomadnetwork','node') for NomadNet pages and ('styrene_node','operator') for Styrene. Devices sharing an identity_hash are the same physical node.

Styrene dual-layer mesh: BATMAN-ADV provides L2 physical connectivity (bat0 virtual switch over 802.11s WiFi, Ethernet, VPN), and Reticulum runs on top as an overlay using bat0 via AutoInterface. RNS.Links then provide encrypted destination-to-destination sessions over whatever transport is available. For nodes connected only via internet TCP (no local BATMAN), RNS.Links through the hub give direct encrypted channels — future work may tunnel L2 frames over these Links to extend the BATMAN domain across the internet, LoRa WAN, WiFi hotspots, and eventually LoRa radios, creating a unified IP mesh that spans all transport types.

Styrene dual-layer mesh architecture confirmed in research docs: BATMAN-ADV (bat0) is the L2 physical layer, Reticulum runs on top via AutoInterface/UDP on bat0. Existing internet TCP connections use RNS.Links through the hub for direct encrypted channels. Future work: tunnel L2 Ethernet frames over RNS.Links to extend BATMAN domain across internet, LoRa WAN, WiFi hotspots, and LoRa radios — creating a unified IP mesh spanning all transport types. See styrene/docs/src/architecture.md and styrene/research/batman-adv.md.

BATMAN-ADV over RNS overlay (future): each Styrene node gets a TAP interface managed by BATMAN-ADV, with RNS.Links serving as virtual point-to-point wires to neighbors. BATMAN-ADV then routes L2 frames across this virtual topology, giving nodes real IP addresses and arbitrary IP services (SSH, HTTP, file shares). Primary use case: extend the bat0 broadcast domain over transport types that don't support native 802.11s (internet TCP, LoRa WAN, WiFi hotspots).

batman-mesh.nix at styrene-edge/sbc/common/ implements 802.11s+BATMAN-ADV for NixOS fleet devices: NetworkManager mesh profile, batctl setup systemd service, configurable meshId/meshKey/channel/gwMode (off/client/server). bat0 is the virtual switch interface exposed to the system.

Current gap in the BATMAN↔internet bridging plan: bat0 L2 domain is local-only (WiFi/Ethernet); internet-connected nodes (TCP to hub) are in a separate L2 domain with no bat0 bridge. RNS.Links exist (DirectLinkService) but carry only Styrene overlay traffic, not raw Ethernet frames. Next step: TAP-over-RNS.Link tunnel to extend bat0 across internet/LoRa transports.
batman-adv and TAP tunneling is Linux-only — a TunnelService extending bat0 over RNS.Links cannot run on macOS (operator workstation). The L2-over-RNS tunnel feature is fleet-device-only.

Styrene mesh VPN architecture: three tiers — (1) Internet → WireGuard to mesh gateway → bat0, (2) Local WiFi → BATMAN-ADV (802.11s) → bat0, (3) LoRa-only → RNS.Link L2 tunnel → bat0. BATMAN-ADV's role is creating IP from raw radios when no infrastructure exists; WireGuard handles the internet-connected tier.

JXL (JPEG XL) accepted as native Styrene image format. Key factors: best compression at ≤50KB (mesh sweet spot), lossless JPEG repack (unique — 20% smaller, bit-exact reversible), progressive decode for slow links, pure Rust decoder (jxl-oxide 0.12, actively maintained), clean BSD-3 license. WebP rejected (less efficient at ≤50KB, no JPEG repack, pure Rust zenwebp only 0.3). AVIF rejected (patent complexity, 3x slower ARM decode, fragmented Rust crates). JPEG accepted as universal fallback.

Image format alternatives assessment completed and documented at styrene-rs/docs/image-format-assessment.md. Rejected: HEIF (patents, no Rust), AVIF (patent complexity, slow ARM decode, fragmented Rust), QOI (worse than JPEG at ≤50KB), FLIF (dead), BPG (dead, H.265 patents), WebP (not best at ≤50KB, no JPEG repack, less mature pure Rust). WebP and JPEG remain accepted receive formats.

macOS nodes (operator workstations) participate in the mesh via RNS over TCP (tier 1 WireGuard gateway path), not via batman-adv. WireGuard to a gateway node bridges into bat0 for IP access. RNS.Link L2 tunneling reserved for LoRa-only nodes with no IP path — the gap WireGuard can't fill.

Mesh VPN tier 1 implementation: use RNS.Link (DirectLinkService) to exchange WireGuard keys and endpoints, then WireGuard handles IP traffic. Gateway nodes bridge wg-styrene into bat0 via batctl. Mac connects via WireGuard to gateway, no batman-adv needed on macOS.

Mesh IP space uses IPv6 ULA (RFC 4193) fd73:7479:7265:6e65::/64. Each node derives its /128 from SHA-256 of RNS identity hash — stable, collision-free, works point-to-point or with BATMAN gateway. When gateway present: Macs route full /64 through it into bat0. When gateway dies: direct /128 routes still work (graceful degradation to point-to-point).

macOS mesh VPN privilege model: call sudo wg-quick up once at VPN start (triggers password prompt at most once per 5min window), then use wg set peer without sudo for all per-peer operations. This avoids repeated prompts as mesh nodes come online.

Mesh VPN handshake uses LXMF protocol (VPN_HANDSHAKE_REQUEST 0x34/VPN_HANDSHAKE_RESPONSE 0x35) not DirectLink RNS.Link requests — hub routes signaling as store-and-forward, no O(n²) direct links needed. Implemented and released in v0.13.33.

Capability implemented as a class with ClassVar[str] constants (not Enum) — string values like 'rpc.exec' for config readability, ClassVar pattern avoids descriptor protocol issues with frozenset construction.

Mesh enclave membership is NOT self-advertised in announces — doing so would defeat anonymity for nodes that want to remain pseudonymous on shared transports. Classification as "my mesh" vs "other/unknown" is derived solely from local RBAC roster membership. An optional out-of-band INFO_REQUEST can be sent to unknown nodes, but receiving nodes must default-deny it (same as all other inbound requests). This is NOT part of the announce protocol.

Capability data sensitivity split: status.request returns only non-identifiable metadata (styrene version, uptime, profile type, capability flags) — nothing that identifies the operator or links the node to an identity. info.request is a separate opt-in capability returning identifiable metadata (node name, operator label, enclave affiliation if chosen). This keeps passive status queries safe for default-allow while identifiable disclosure remains explicit default-deny. Applies to both RPC STATUS_REQUEST and DirectLink /status handler.

info_respond config flag (default false) on DiscoveryConfig controls whether /info DirectLink handler serves identifiable node metadata — default-deny silent empty-dict response, explicit opt-in required. operator_label field also on DiscoveryConfig.

For 'my mesh' classification, check identity_hash explicitly in RBACPolicy.roster with role >= PEER using config.rbac.resolve_role(identity_hash) — resolve_role() does prefix-match blocked first, then roster lookup, then default_role fallback, so default_role=PEER would classify all nodes as mine.

Dashboard mesh split fix strategy: store both destination_hash and identity_hash in tree node.data (e.g., as tuple or dataclass), or maintain a separate dict[destination_hash, identity_hash] on MeshDeviceTree. This is the root fix for all comparison/cache-key mismatches. Robustness and security primary focus over performance.

_format_other_line 'gave up' state: when _meta_fail_count[identity_hash] > 0 and no meta cached, no suffix is shown (pass statement). Node displays with just the truncated identity hash — no pending indicator and no error text.

Datalink response validation strategy: validate at the DirectLinkService layer (not dashboard), so all callers receive pre-sanitized dicts. _validate_meta_response/_validate_info_response are the canonical trust boundary for external node data.

Security priority ladder for remaining RBAC phases: Phase 2a — wire RBACPolicy.resolve_role() into RPCServer._is_authorized() to fix fail-open; Phase 2b — wire into TerminalService; Phase 2c — wire into WebAuth; Phase 3 — switch DirectLink /ping /meta /info /speedtest from ALLOW_ALL to ALLOW_LIST using RBACPolicy.get_allow_list(); Phase 4 — replace LXMF banned_peers prefix list with RBACPolicy BLOCKED role. Each phase is ~1 session. Phase 2a is highest risk due to RPC fail-open+exec.

However if two peers somehow share the same VNI with different remote addresses on the same VXLAN namespace, kernel behavior varies. The point-to-point (unicast remote) configuration avoids multicast but VNI isolation between Styrene fleets using same VNI is absent.

RBAC Security Migration Plan — 6 critical paths in strict dependency order. PATH 1 (Phase 2): Replace RPCServer._is_authorized() with rbac.has_capability() per StyreneMessageType. Map: PING→PING, STATUS_REQUEST→STATUS_QUERY, EXEC→EXEC, REBOOT→REBOOT, CONFIG_UPDATE→CONFIG_UPDATE, SELF_UPDATE→SELF_UPDATE, INBOX_QUERY/MESSAGES_QUERY→new INBOX_READ (MONITOR+), TERMINAL_REQUEST→TERMINAL_RESTRICTED/FULL. Remove enable_dangerous_commands and authorized_identities from RPCServer. Split _gather_status() response by role (MONITOR+ full, PEER meta-only) same as DirectLink. Risk: RPC path bypasses all DirectLink hardening — any node can query inbox/status over LXMF.

RBAC PATH 2 (Phase 2, same session as PATH 1): Replace LXMFService._is_blocked() with rbac.resolve_role()==BLOCKED. Keep contacts.blocked as UI state but have TUI block action write to RBAC roster. Migrate config.banned_peers→rbac.blocked[] (migration code exists in services/config.py but not enforced). RBAC blocked check must fire before any protocol dispatch in _on_message_received. Risk: blocked peers can still deliver LXMF messages if not in contacts DB; RBAC blocklist and contacts blocklist diverge silently.

RBAC PATH 3 (Phase 3, depends on Phase 2): Switch all 5 DirectLink handlers from ALLOW_ALL to ALLOW_LIST. Minimum roles: /meta /ping → PEER+, /info → PEER+ AND info_respond, /status → PEER+ (MONITOR+ for full data), /speedtest → MONITOR+. Use rbac.get_allow_list(cap) for RNS allowed_list and rbac.should_use_allow_all(cap) when default_role>=PEER. Re-register handlers on roster change. Keep app-layer rate limiter as defense-in-depth. Risk: link-level resource exhaustion — any identity can establish persistent encrypted links consuming memory/path-table.

RBAC PATH 4+5 (Phase 4): Terminal — replace TerminalService.is_authorized() with rbac.has_capability(TERMINAL_RESTRICTED/FULL), remove authorized_identities and allow_unauthenticated from TerminalConfig. Web API — replace challenge() identity check with rbac.has_capability(WEB_READ/WEB_WRITE), remove authorized_identities and allow_unauthenticated from APIAuthConfig. Risk: three independent identity whitelists (RPC, Terminal, Web) with divergent failure modes.

RBAC PATH 6 (Phase 5, v0.15.0): Remove all legacy config fields — rpc.authorized_identities, rpc.enable_dangerous_commands, terminal.authorized_identities, terminal.allow_unauthenticated, api.auth.authorized_identities, api.auth.allow_unauthenticated, banned_peers. Migration path _migrate_legacy_to_rbac already exists in services/config.py. Breaking config change → major version bump. Execution order: PATH 1+2 (Phase 2) → PATH 3 (Phase 3) → PATH 4+5 (Phase 4) → PATH 6 (Phase 5).

RBAC critical context for all phases: 6 independent auth surfaces exist today — DirectLink (ALLOW_ALL + rate limiter + app-layer RBAC on /status), RPC (authorized_identities + enable_dangerous_commands + rate_limit), Terminal (authorized_identities + allow_unauthenticated), Web API (authorized_identities + allow_unauthenticated + RNS challenge-response), LXMF (contacts.blocked + banned_peers). PUBLIC_RPC_COMMANDS = {PING, STATUS_REQUEST} bypass auth entirely. DANGEROUS_RPC_COMMANDS = {EXEC, REBOOT, CONFIG_UPDATE, SELF_UPDATE}. title: Documented RBAC Security Migration Plan Across 6 Auth Surfaces
narrative: The goal was to map and preserve the full RBAC security migration plan for styrened, which had been worked out in-session analyzing all 6 independent authorization surfaces (RPC, LXMF, DirectLink, Terminal, Web API, and legacy config). The analysis identified that Phase 1 RBAC policy model was built but not yet wired into any enforcement point, with RPC being the most critical gap (fail-open, bypasses DirectLink hardening). Six ordered paths were defined with exact method targets, capability mappings, and risk assessments. All plan details were persisted to Graphiti memory across 6 entries so a new session can reconstruct the full dependency chain. The immediate next work is Phase 2: PATH 1 (RPCServer._is_authorized() → rbac.has_capability()) and PATH 2 (LXMFService._is_blocked() → rbac.resolve_role()) in a single session.

title: Fixed critical IPC enum collision, audit issues, added 28 tests
narrative: The goal was to resolve a critical IPC command value collision where datalink commands (0x60-range intended) overlapped with terminal commands (0x50-range), causing Python's IntEnum to silently alias duplicates and misroute messages. The collision was fixed by relocating datalink commands to 0x60-0x64, and a regression test was added asserting all IPCMessageType values are unique. Alongside the critical fix, a full audit sweep addressed eight additional issues: DirectLinkService.stop() added to daemon shutdown, bridge variable initialized before try/except to prevent UnboundLocalError, _resolve() race condition patched with try/except, status cache bounded to 64 entries with LRU eviction, speedtest guarded with asyncio.Lock, bar chart scaling made relative, and dead variables removed. Twenty-eight new unit tests were written covering RTT-adaptive payload selection, cache TTL and eviction, service lifecycle, exploration table state, and the IPC collision regression. The release was tagged v0.13.29 and published to PyPI; a Dependabot high-severity alert on the repo remains open.

title: TUI screen stack dedup and r-key update check fix
narrative: The goal was to fix two TUI bugs: screen overlays stacking duplicates (double-ESC behavior) and the 'r' refresh key never triggering the version update check. The `action_open_*` guards used `isinstance(self.screen, T)` which only checks the top of the stack, so a new `_screen_in_stack(T)` helper was introduced to scan the full stack. `action_refresh()` was updated to also call `_check_for_updates()`, which is safe due to its `@work(exclusive=True)` decorator. Pre-existing uncommitted changes from a prior session (WireGuard handshake improvements, direct_link teardown hardening, daemon lifecycle, and 20 new mesh VPN tests) were batched into the same commit. All changes were released as v0.13.32 to both PyPI and GHCR.

title: TUI Chat Widget and Dashboard Deep Audit
narrative: The session was a detailed code review of a styrened TUI patch targeting chat widget improvements, clipboard handling, dashboard data display, and mesh hop tracking. The reviewer systematically traced data flows through RNS transport internals, IPC handlers, Textual widget lifecycle, and CSS layout to identify bugs. The audit found six critical issues including an incomplete NSPasteboard threading fix still present in paste paths, non-existent dict keys causing permanently blank TRAFFIC stats, a missing NodeStore method silently zeroing contact counts, incremental refresh not handling message deletion, and multiple concurrent dashboard worker races. Twelve additional warnings and omissions were documented, including no persistence for the new hops field and no tests for any new UI behaviors. The verdict was NEEDS REWORK.
